stem.text: The function \( f \) is differentiable on the closed interval \( [0, 8] \), and its derivative is \( f'(x) = (x - 3)e^{-x} \).

parts.prompt: Find the open interval on which \( f \) is decreasing. Show the analysis that leads to your answer.

worked_solution.text: The exponential factor is positive, so f' has the sign of x - 3.

points.criterion: Gives the interval (0, 3), supported by the sign of x - 3 with e^{-x} positive.

parts.prompt: Find the value of \( x \) at which \( f \) attains its absolute minimum on the closed interval \( [0, 8] \). Justify your answer.

worked_solution.text: f' is negative on (0, 3) and positive on (3, 8).
x = 3 is the only critical point in the interval, so f falls to f(3) and rises after it.

points.criterion: Gives x = 3 with supporting sign analysis.

Justifies with the sign of f' on each side of x = 3 (negative on (0, 3), positive on (3, 8)) and a global statement, such as x = 3 being the only critical point on the interval or f decreasing on all of [0, 3] and increasing on all of [3, 8].
